expectations.text: Flags Card's `shadow` prop as not existing on the component, verified against docs rather than assumed
expectations.evidence: The `shadow="lg"` prop on Card is never mentioned anywhere in the baseline review — no Hearth docs were consulted so there was no way to know it doesn't exist.

expectations.text: Flags the raw px `style={{ padding: '16px' }}` as bypassing the token system
expectations.evidence: Item 2: 'Hardcoded 16px is a magic number rather than a token reference... the value should come from the same spacing scale.'

expectations.text: Flags `marginRight` used for spacing between siblings instead of `gap` on the parent Flex
expectations.evidence: Item 1 groups `marginRight="100"`/`marginLeft="auto"` with the *good* prop-based pattern, contrasted favourably against the inline `style` usage ('prefer those consistently instead of hardcoded style objects') — it does not identify margin-on-sibling itself as the anti-pattern, since it has no knowledge that Hearth's own convention is `gap` on the parent instead.

expectations.text: Flags `<Heading>` missing the `as` prop as an accessibility gap
expectations.evidence: Item 5: 'No explicit heading level. `<Heading>Account summary</Heading>` doesn't specify a level (e.g. `as="h2"`)...'

Item 4: '...it should be marked `aria-hidden="true"` (or the equivalent prop the icon component exposes); if it's meant to convey urgency/warning semantics on its own, it needs an explicit accessible label.' — recommends action, unlike the with-skill run.

expectations.text: Flags the CSS variable string in the `style` prop as should be a browser token instead
expectations.evidence: Item 3: 'if the component library has a themed "surface"/"background" prop that accepts token names, using it directly would be safer than referencing the CSS variable by string.'

expectations.text: Flags `marginLeft="auto"` as a margin hack that should be `justifyContent` on the Flex wrapper
expectations.evidence: Same as the marginRight finding above — `marginLeft="auto"` is grouped with the 'good' prop-based pattern, not identified as a margin-hack anti-pattern needing `justifyContent` instead.

expectations.text: Findings are grouped into tiers rather than presented as a flat list
expectations.evidence: Grouped under category headings (Styling/tokens, Accessibility, Component API/data handling, Minor/consistency) with a closing Summary distinguishing 'two biggest things worth fixing' from 'lower priority' — not a flat list, though not the skill's specific Tier 1/2/3 structure.

expectations.text: Does not report every prop usage as an error — correct usage is left unflagged
expectations.evidence: Card/CardContent/Flex/onClick usage is never flagged as incorrect; findings are limited to genuine concerns.

eval_feedback.overall: No eval-quality issues distinct from the with-skill run's feedback.
